articles.author: Amrith Setlur
articles.description: LLM RL typically operates in one of three exploration regimes: sharpening, chaining, or guided exploration; standard RL stays in the first two and plateaus on hard problems, even those in the training set. Mixing easy and hard data triggers interference, causing reward-rich tasks to drown out hard ones and stall exploration. Our approach (POPE) pushes RL into the guided regime by conditioning on prefixes from offline human data while keeping updates fully on-policy. This lets RL reliably find reward on problems previously unsolved without falling prey to the optimization issues suffered by methods that directly supervise offline traces.

Agentic sabotage occurs when an AI system intentionally takes actions that compromise safety in an environment while pursuing its own misaligned objectives. We evaluate this behavior in SHADE-Arena, a dataset for assessing sabotage and monitoring capabilities of LLM agents. We decompose agentic sabotage capability into five core components—knowing what overseers find suspicious, selecting good moments to attack, writing effective plans, strong execution, and framing suspicious actions as innocuous—which together form a scaffold that amplifies an agent’s sabotage abilities. Each component is optimized and analyzed through targeted techniques, enabled by a probabilistic model of SHADE-Arena dynamics that allows for efficient experimentation. Our tuned scaffold results in a substantial improvement in sabotage ability for Claude 3.7 Sonnet in SHADE-Arena, reducing safety score from a baseline of 0.87 to 0.41.
